reasons: No tests are visible for this file.
Old .doc and .ppt formats are listed but cannot be read.
Parser errors are not caught here.

terms.meaning: the Outlook archive file format that holds a whole mailbox
an optional library needed to read PST files, which can be hard to install

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports and optional PST support
sections.what: Brings in every parser and tries to load the PST parser. If its library is missing, the app notes that PST support is off instead of failing.
sections.why: Likely reason: pypff is hard to install on some computers, so it is optional. The code comment says so.
sections.watch_out: Only a missing-import failure is handled here, so any other error inside the PST module would still stop start-up.

sections.name: ParserManager
sections.title: Parser selection and parsing
sections.what: Creates the list of parsers at start-up, picks the first one that accepts a file, runs it, and reports the supported endings.
sections.why: Likely reason: one place decides which reader to use. Reason not stated.
sections.watch_out: Only the first matching parser runs, so the order of the list matters.

summary: Picks the right parser for a file, runs it, and reports which file types the app can read.
purpose: Gives the rest of the app one place to ask whether a file can be read and to read it.
why: Likely reason: callers should not need to know which parser handles which format. Reason not stated.
how: At start-up it creates one parser for each supported group of formats and adds the PST parser if its library loaded. For a given file, it asks each parser in turn whether it can read the file, and the first one that says yes does the work. If no parser matches, it logs a warning and returns an empty list. It can also list every supported file ending.
outputs: A list of parsed records, or an empty list. Also yes or no answers and a list of supported file endings.
risks: Word .doc and PowerPoint .ppt files are listed as supported, but their libraries read only the newer formats. Errors from a parser are passed up, so one bad file can stop a batch unless the caller handles it. The supported endings come from a set, so their order is random.
debug: Look for the Using line in the log to see which parser was picked. If PST files are skipped, look for the warning that pypff is missing. If a file is ignored, look for the warning that no parser was available.
